newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP has 18 mth capital plan for NZ Steel.
newsitem.headline: BHP has 18 mth capital plan for NZ Steel.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to improve the financial performance of its NZ Steel unit by the end of calendar 1998.
BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly said the 750,000 tonne a year unit was achieving a single digit return on capital at the moment.

"And our objective there is to drive that return in the next 18 months up to double digits. But that is a challenge," McNeilly told a news conference called to explain the company's steel division restructuring in Australia and overseas.
Asked if the NZ steelmaking facilities would close sooner than the 10 year timeframe outlined in an earlier statement, he said: "We want to really drive that business hard."
The NZ unit had assets of a little more than A$800 million and its valuation was justified in cash flow terms.

"But again to be very specific we do not see that the replacement of the .. existing technology could be justified as these facilities reach the end of their life which we now see as being no more than 10 years," McNeilly said.
